title: upgrade: attention kernels -> FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops + ROPE/rotary optimizations, KV continuous batching & scheduler tuning
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Motivation: Upgrade the attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 (FA2) with fused rotary/ROPE-supporting ops and targeted KV-cache batching/scheduler tuning to reduce tail latency and increase GPU throughput for long-context serving. This PR brings FA2 integration, a set of fused ops for rotary/rope application, and runtime knobs for continuous KV batching and scheduling fallbacks. The changes are behind a runtime feature flag (runtime.attn.kernel=auto|fa2|legacy) and gated by canary rollout.

What this PR does: - Integrates FlashAttentionV2 kernels with our runtime operator interface. - Adds fused pre/post-rotary ops to reduce memory bandwidth and kernel launch overhead. - Introduces continuous KV batching path that aggregates KV inserts for small requests and flushes based on GPU occupancy heuristics. - Scheduler tuning: better binning of requests by seq_len and priority, avoid starvation of small latency-sensitive requests. - Adds runtime config, diagnostics, and a safe fallback to legacy kernels if FA2 fails at runtime.

Benchmarks (canary clusters, p95 measured): - Llama-2 13B (gen 1024 tokens): p95 latency reduced from 210ms -> 156ms (-25.7%), throughput (tokens/s) +1.45x. - MPT-30B mixed workload: mean GPU utilization improved 12%, memory transient allocs reduced ~18%. - KV-heavy chat workload (many short updates): end-to-end p99 improved 18% with continuous batching enabled. See ci/perf artifacts for full tables and flamegraphs.

Compatibility & safety: - FA2 is opt-in via runtime.attn.kernel; default for canary = fa2, default for global = auto which prefers fa2 when supported. - Added runtime integrity checks and a hot fallback to legacy kernels on kernel errors. - No model-format changes required.

Testing & rollout: - Unit tests for fused ops and kernel selection. - Integration perf tests in perf-canary and perf-lab. - Gradual canary rollout (20% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on perf regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Kernel integration and operator bindings - [x] Fused ROPE/rotary ops implemented - [x] Continuous KV batching path + heuristics - [x] Scheduler tuning and config knobs - [x] Perf tests and canary pipeline - [x] Documentation and release notes

Related: earlier attention kernel upgrades and experiments (see PRs: #613579, #624999, #589001). Linear: ENG-4217 (attention kernel revamp), ENG-4258 (kv batching heuristics).

Notes for reviewers: Focus on correctness of fused rotary math, memory reclamation paths in kv_cache manager, and scheduler backoff behavior. The implementation tries to minimize branching in the hot path and keep fallbacks low-cost.

review_comments: Marco Chen: Can we add an assert to validate rotary scaling when using fused ops? I saw small numerical diffs on FP16 rounding in the perf runs.
Aisha Patel: Added validate_rotary_scale() and an fp16 tolerance path. Updated tests to include a deterministic seed for fp16 checks.
Zoe Martinez: Scheduler change looks good, but please add a comment explaining the starvation protection heuristic.
Aisha Patel: Expanded comments and added a unit test that simulates a high volume of small low-priority requests.
Daniel Kim: CI perf check flagged an outlier on one node; was that an infra flake?
Aisha Patel: That was an infra noise; re-ran the perf job and results were consistent. CI artifact linked in the checks.
Marco Chen: Approve after small nits fixed.
release_notes: Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels with fused ROPE/rotary ops, add continuous KV batching and scheduler improvements. Expected: ~25% p95 latency reduction for long-context workloads and ~1.4x throughput improvement in typical generation workloads. Feature gated and canary-rolled; opt-out via runtime.attn.kernel=legacy.
canary_plan: 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on perf regressions; monitor p95/p99, GPU utilization, and kv_cache growth metrics
notes: This PR refactors some operator registration paths; keep an eye on third-party kernel version mismatch on older CUDA drivers. We added compatibility tests and fallbacks.
